correctness.rationale: The exact least-squares decomposition gives independent chi-square and normal components, and the unbounded update is a shifted-normal simple pole plus a faster Student tail. Conditional interval shrinking and integrable domination prove the sharp 1/t coefficient. The gamma integral gives its explicit constant; tail integration and inverse-normal estimates prove the complete q moment spectrum. The gradient-ridge algebra reduces to a normal |u|/(u²+a²) integral; a logarithmic local expansion and chi-square domination prove the leading half-tail coefficient. Fresh independent calibrated updates give an AR(1) of scaled Student innovations, yielding its exact stationary q-moment threshold and variance. The standard-library verifier replays 690 exact rational batch identities, 12 independent chi-square quadratures, 16 stationary variance algebra tests and diagnostic sampling. Finite tests are not used to infer the infinite claims.

value.rationale: Provides an exact, natural numerical risk invariant for a widely motivated adaptive stepsize under positive residual/noisy batches: the coefficient, ridge log cost and batch moment boundary quantify a sharp distinction between valid lower-bounding and exact residual subtraction. The contrast shows why arbitrarily increasing finite batch size does not eliminate a rare-gradient instability. Nontrivial sharp constants and a calibrated stationary risk comparison can inform adaptation/safeguard design; this is not a generic positive-definite textbook reduction.
